title: Incremental RBAC v2 orchestration and customer-safe cutover
creator: Asha Raman
description: Goal: Perform a low-risk, observable migration from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 using an incremental dual-write, near-real-time backfill, and a staged cutover that preserves audit continuity and SSO role mappings. Emphasis on operational runbooks, automated reconciliation, and explicit customer-facing safeguards (opt-in grace period and rollback hooks).
background: RBAC v2 introduces a normalized role/permission model and canonical role IDs for multi-tenant mappings. Past migrations identified three failure modes: stale mappings after backfill, missing audit context when switching stores, and SSO role-mapping discrepancies for IdP-initiated flows. This ticket coordinates orchestration, validation, comms, and rollback safeguards for a multi-week migration window.
migration_plan: Phase 0 (Preflight, 2 weeks): schema migration dry-run in staging; smoke-tests for token/permission checks; verify audit export/import; run SSO mapping simulator against sample IdPs.

Phase 1 (Dual-write + permissive reads, 1 week): enable dual-write from API layer to RBAC v1 and RBAC v2. Reads continue to use v1. Dual-write telemetry is validated and reconciler collects divergence metrics.
Phase 2 (Backfill ramp, 2 weeks): run prioritized backfill jobs by tenancy size (low->high). Each tenant backfill gated by reconciliation pass and audit confidence metric (see acceptance criteria).

Phase 3 (Canary reads, 1 week): flip reads to v2 for selected canary tenants (5% of active production accounts, prioritizing internal/test tenants). Monitor errors, authorization failures, and audit gaps for 48h before expanding.

Phase 4 (Full read cutover, 3 days): schedule cutover window per region with customer notices and immediate rollback capability. Post-cutover, deprecate v1 read paths after 14-day grace and final reconciliation.
backfill_strategy: Backfill jobs will run in tenant-sized batches with backpressure limits to avoid spikes to the auth datastore and identity providers.
Confidence criterion: reconciliation mismatch rate <= 0.01% for 24h, no P0 auth incidents, and audit log parity checks passing for sampled sessions.
Backfill will preserve original role assignment timestamps and origin metadata to ensure audit continuity.
Long-running backfills will checkpoint state to S3 and emit progress metrics (tenants_completed, items_processed, errors).
dual_write_details: Implementation: API service will write to both RBAC v1 and v2 via a write adapter. Writes are idempotent and stamped with `migration_run_id` and `source_trace` headers.
Visibility: dual_write_success and dual_write_latency exposed via existing service metrics. Failure streams go to a dedicated kinesis topic `rbac-migration-failures` for triage.
Edge cases: conflict resolution uses v2-preferred last-writer-wins with tombstone semantics to avoid resurrecting deleted bindings.
Operational control: feature flag `rbac.v2.dual_write.enabled` with rollout control in console for Dedicated/Private customers.
cutover_checklist: 1) Confirm dual-write steady-state: dual_write_success >= 99.9% over 72h and no elevated authorization errors.
2) Audit parity: daily audit export comparison shows event-level parity for sampled sessions (1000 sessions across tenants).
3) SSO mapping verification: run IdP replay tests for top 50 customers and confirm role mapping match rates >= 99.5%.
4) Run canary: flip reads for 5% tenants; observe metrics for 48h. If any P0 auth failure or audit gap occurs, rollback reads immediately.
5) Customer notices: send targeted comms to customers in canary with opt-out instructions and support contacts.
6) Have rollback runbook open and assignee on-call during cutover.
7) Post-cutover: schedule final reconciliation job and a deprecation announcement for v1 read endpoints.
rollback_plan: Rollback trigger conditions: sustained auth error rate > 0.1% above baseline, any customer-reported P0 auth outage, or audit parity failure for 1h.
Rollback steps: flip reads back to v1 via feature flag within 5 minutes; pause backfill jobs; push immediate notification to SRE and PM; create incident and attach migration-run logs.
Post-rollback validation: ensure all active sessions authorized under v1, re-run SSO mapping checks, and run full reconciliation for affected tenants.
Follow-ups: triage root cause, adjust backfill/dual-write logic, and schedule a new cutover window after remediation.
monitoring_and_alerts: Authorization error budget: alert if auth_failures_per_min > baseline + 0.1% for 10m.
Dual-write lag metric: alert if `rbac.v2.write_lag` > 30s for 5m.
Audit-forwarding gap: alert if last-audit-forwarded-timestamp older than 1h in any region.
Reconciliation dashboard widgets: per-tenant divergence rate, time-to-converge histogram, top failing keys, and SSO-mapping mismatch rate.
Playbook links: link to runbook for `rbac-migration-auth-failure` responders and SRE escalation matrix.
communications: Internal: Weekly sync with PM, Security, SRE, and Developer Docs. Post daily migration notes to #rbac-migration Slack channel during active phases.
External (customers): staged email cadence - preflight notice (2w prior), canary invite (1w prior), cutover notice (48h prior), and post-cutover summary with rollback window info.
Support: updated KB article with how to opt out, how to test role mappings in Console, and diagnostic steps to collect for support tickets.
Legal/Compliance: notify customers on dedicated/private plans with separate SLAs and provide audit export template on request.
open_risks: SSO mapping edge cases for older IdP setups that use non-standard attributes could cause missing role assertions.
Large tenants with many bindings may extend backfill windows and increase the chance of transient inconsistencies.
Audit continuity risk during the brief switch of authoritative store if export/import has a timing gap.
decisions: Decision 2026-02-25: prefer canary-first approach (5% tenants) vs. region-first. Rationale: reduces blast radius and simplifies SSO replay testing.
Decision 2026-03-03: adopt v2-last-writer-wins tombstone policy to simplify reconcile logic and avoid resurrecting deletions.
Decision 2026-03-08: require security review sign-off prior to canary reads.
